topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Scaling Dimensions
lecture_lines: We study geometry beyond three dimensions.
Distance in n-dimensions follows the Pythagorean theorem.
The sphere equation generalizes as sum of squares.
animations: Create a 2D plane labeled '#FFFFFF' and then transform it to a 3D space labeled '#FFFF00'.
Animate a line segment showing the distance formula sqrt(x^2 + y^2) evolving into sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) with labels in '#00FF00'.
Display the sphere equation x^2+y^2+z^2=r^2 in '#FF00FF' and generalize it to sum(xi^2)=r^2, visualizing this with [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive 'Spiky' Sphere
lecture_lines: As dimensions increase, sphere volume shrinks to zero.
Surprisingly, volume migrates to the thin outer shell.
Imagine an orange with almost no pulp.
animations: Animate a sphere shrinking as the number of dimensions increases, shown with a label 'Volume -> 0' in '#FF0000'.
Visualize a sphere expanding its boundary layer, highlighting the outer shell in '#00FFFF'.
Show a cross-section of an [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg] where the pulp area, labeled '#FFA500', is shrinking towards zero.

sections.title: The Corner Problem: Cubes vs. Spheres
lecture_lines: Compare a hypercube to an inscribed hypersphere.
High-dimensional volume accumulates in the cube's corners.
The sphere occupies a tiny fraction of the cube.
animations: Display a 2D square with an inscribed circle, then transition to a 3D [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] with an inscribed [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] in '#00FF00'.

Show the ratio of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] volume to [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] volume shrinking towards zero in '#FF0000'.

sections.title: Practical Application: Data Science and AI
lecture_lines: Data science often deals with many dimensions.
High-dimensional points appear almost equidistant from each other.
This complicates clustering and pattern recognition.
animations: Show a scatter plot of data points in a 2D coordinate system with points in '#00FFFF'.
Animate the points drifting apart until they all appear equidistant in '#FFFFFF'.
Draw a cluster circle in '#FF00FF' that struggles to contain the spreading data points.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: High-dimensional space is remarkably hollow and spiky.
Our 3D intuition fails at higher dimensions.
Geometry behaves differently in these strange realms.
